item.title: Former Texas teacher admits stealing $520,000 in tax refunds as $4m more is stopped
item.description: In a shocking turn of events, former Texas teacher Jeremy Jarod Jackson confessed to orchestrating a scheme that siphoned off $520,000 in tax refunds. He masterfully altered his company's mailing address to funnel cheques into his own hands, triggering extensive financial wrongdoing. Luckily, IRS Criminal Investigation agents intervened, blocking Jackson from cashing in on an additional $4 million in fraudulent cheques.

item.title: A West Texas family wanted its ranchland to become part of Big Bend National Park; a US House panel has advanced a bill allowing about 6,100 acres to be added through voluntary donation or exchange
item.description: The Congress is exploring the Big Bend National Park Boundary Adjustment Act, which proposes to extend the park by incorporating 6,100 acres from the Fulcher family's ranch. The Big Bend Conservancy plans to acquire this land to enhance conservation efforts and safeguard its ecological importance. This boundary expansion aims to protect vital habitats and historical landmarks, emphasizing the value of preserving lands with rich familial and historical narratives.

item.title: Federal Lawsuit: Union sues New York City to block carriage ban; owners seek compensation
item.description: In a groundbreaking move, New York City has decided to phase out the horse-drawn carriage industry by June 2028, prompted by safety concerns highlighted by the tragic case of Romanch, a tourist fatally injured in an accident. The Transport Workers Union of America has responded with a lawsuit, claiming the new legislation jeopardizes their livelihoods.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: A Texas cliff has yielded evidence that Indigenous communities drove bison over its edge repeatedly
item.description: Recent archaeological discoveries have uncovered that Indigenous peoples utilized cliffs as bison jumps for millennia. The Nighthawk site in Texas showcases bison remains from various hunting events, demonstrating the importance of these communal hunts in shaping social and political dynamics within communities. Evidence also indicates that hunters revisited this site across generations, refining their tools and strategies, challenging previous assumptions about bison hunting in the Southern Plains.
item.dc:creator: World Desk

item.title: Rodin's The Thinker jumps from $192,500 to $7.928m after 41 years off market
item.description: The auction at Christie's on November 17 witnessed a remarkable highlight with the sale of Rodin's 1955 sculpture, Le Penseur, for a staggering $7.928 million, reflecting a dramatic price increase since its 1985 auction. This notable sculpture, which had not changed hands in 41 years, underscores the strong appetite for fine art in a week when total sales at Christie's neared $974 million.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Birmingham teen wins Alibaba's $200,000 prize for his self-taught robotics business
item.description: Suleymaan Khan, a brilliant self-taught robotics engineer hailing from Birmingham, has made waves at CoCreate Europe by securing a prestigious award. As the founder of SuleyNova Robotics, he created innovative educational robotics kits aimed at teaching coding and engineering concepts. Out of 20,000 competitors globally, the top 20 were chosen to pitch their inventions.

item.title: Ohio court protects homeowners' lakeside peninsula from a company's land claim after a 2019 survey
item.description: An Ohio court has definitively ruled that homeowners can retain their claim to a lakeside peninsula amid contentious property disputes. This decision followed a challenge from 1643 Limited LLC, which sought to redefine its property borders based on a 2019 survey. Although the appeals court confirmed the company's ownership of the adjacent beach, it firmly denied its rights over the peninsula itself, requiring a narrowed property description for the LLC.

item.title: San Diego 60-apartment project stalled; appeals court allows property owners' lawsuit to proceed
item.description: In San Diego, a family-owned auto-repair business encounters legal turmoil over an apartment development project that has stalled. The conflict arose from financial disagreements and allegations of misrepresentation between the original property owners and the developer. E&N, Inc. has taken legal action against Daniel Haas and his associates, and the court has determined that the case must proceed in litigation rather than arbitration, keeping E&N's claims alive for future resolution.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Mike Alstott's foundation delivers Thanksgiving meals to firefighters
item.description: As the Thanksgiving holiday approached, Mike Alstott's Family Foundation distributed meals to firefighters in Hillsborough County. This annual gesture aims to make their holiday shift less lonely and more special. Each meal package included traditional Thanksgiving foods such as turkey, stuffing, and dessert for shared celebrations. Alstott emphasized the importance of thanking first responders who dedicate their time to community safety.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: California woman wins half of ex-husband's pension earned during 10 years before marriage
item.description: In a landmark decision, California resident Lisa Seiwald has successfully claimed half of her ex-partner Nicholas Irias's pension benefits accrued during their years together. This ruling, affirmed by a California appeals court, reinforces her legal rights concerning shared financial assets despite Irias's arguments related to pension protections under state law. The case underscores the importance of recognizing arrangements made by couples in domestic partnerships.

item.title: Cost Assessment: Heat pumps add $12,526 upfront; officials weigh changes before 2029
item.description: In California's Bay Area, homeowners will face steeper expenses when upgrading from natural gas heating systems due to stringent new emissions regulations. Transitioning to electric heat pumps is projected to cost around $12,526 for an average single-family residence. Although this adjustment aims to curtail nitrogen oxide emissions from gas furnaces, effective January 1, 2029, long-term energy savings may offset the initial investment.
